per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover Personal Care Services for beneficiaries who live in an assisted living facility?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes — NC Medicaid can cover Personal Care Services for a beneficiary who lives in an assisted living facility, but only if the person meets the policy’s congregate-setting PCS criteria.

Under Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Medicaid covers PCS for a beneficiary who resides in “a congregate facility licensed by the State of North Carolina as an Adult Care Home (ACH)” or certain licensed group homes, and who also meets the required functional and medical criteria. That includes beneficiaries living in an assisted-living-type adult care setting if the facility is one of the licensed congregate settings described in the policy. [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings, § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

Coverage is not automatic. The same policy says PCS is not covered if, for example, the beneficiary does not meet the policy criteria, the required assessment has not been completed, the service is provided somewhere other than the beneficiary’s primary congregate living setting, family or informal caregivers are available to meet the need, or the service exceeds the authorized amount. [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings, § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment); [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings, § 4.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

A key limitation: Medicaid PCS in this setting does not include room and board. [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings, § 4.2.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

I checked amendments for Policy 3L-1 and did not find any change notice replacing it in the corpus, so 3L-1 is the current authoritative document for this question. If you want, I can also break down the exact eligibility criteria for getting PCS in an assisted living facility.

scores.explanation: The agent's answer is factually accurate, correctly identifying Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1 as governing PCS in congregate settings, correctly citing section 3.2.1 for eligibility criteria (ACH or qualified group home residency plus functional/medical criteria), section 4.1/4.2 for non-coverage conditions, and section 4.2.1.2 for the room and board exclusion. Citations are precise at the section level. No hallucinations are present - all claims are supported by the evidence. The answer is slightly less complete than the reference in that it does not detail the specific ADL thresholds (e.g., three of five qualifying ADLs with limited hands-on assistance, two ADLs with extensive assistance, etc.) or enumerate the full list of covered PCS services under section 3.3, but it captures the core policy framework well. A Medicaid policy expert would find this answer accurate and useful, though somewhat less detailed than optimal regarding the specific functional criteria thresholds.
